issue: Push has no deadline, `PushOptions` or callbacks. `remote.push` passes `None` (`ddb-core/src/git_ops/remote.rs:70-77`), and the push path in `remote.rs` has no wall-clock deadline. Push relies only on the process-global libgit2 idle timeout. A remote that trickles bytes, or any transport the idle timeout does not cover, never aborts a push. Fetch has the same gap before any progress callback fires, for example a slowly dribbled ref advertisement. The spec requires an abort-capable mechanism, `FetchOptions`/`PushOptions`, and one options/credentials construction point for 00191. Fetch installs callbacks and push installs none.
reason: Scoped out by the reviewed design doc on purpose: git2-rs's push_transfer_progress/pack_progress are void FnMuts and cannot abort, so push's bound is the bidirectional libgit2 idle timeout. The design states the residual trickle-only push gap explicitly and instructs the implementor not to close it in this PRD. Deferred to batch end as a known limitation, not re-argued per cycle.

issue: Silent-stall protection is installed only by server startup. CLI/FFI callers use the changed core operations without installing these options; push's timeout argument only classifies errors after return and cannot terminate a stall. Initialize default native timeouts safely for supported standalone callers, without adding a CLI knob.
reason: The PRD's success metric is explicit: "No CLI/FFI change". Installing process-global libgit2 timeouts from core would change CLI and FFI behaviour, which this PRD forbids; the server is the only configured consumer. Deferred to batch end as a follow-up decision rather than reversing a stated PRD boundary mid-cycle.
